jobs.title: Director, Personal Lines, Business Planning & Performance
jobs.description:
Job ID:
10365

Employment Type:
Existing Role

Work Environment:
We offer a hybrid work environment that offers flexibility to our employees in balancing in-office (2 days per week OR 15 hours per week in a Wawanesa office) and remote work. You may work from any of the following locations: Winnipeg, MB; Calgary, AB; oronto (North York), ON; Kitchener.

Working Business Language
: English

Salary:
At Wawanesa, salary is only one component of a holistic, comprehensive and competitive offering that we provide to our employees. In addition to salary, full-time and part-time permanent employees are eligible for an annual bonus plan, leave of absence top-up programs and provided with generous vacation time, personal days, premium free benefits and pension plan.

The salary offered for this role is determined with consideration to various factors, including but not limited to: your work location, local labour market conditions, external market salary data, internal pay equity and the knowledge, skills, experience and anticipated proficiency in the role. The salary offered is estimated to be within the following range: $120,000 - $140,000. Candidates with salary expectations outside of the range are still encouraged to apply.

About The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company

Founded in 1896, The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company is one of Canada’s largest mutual insurers, fully owned by its more than 1.8 million members. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Wawanesa is the parent company of WSI™, a specialty insurer delivering tailored solutions built around unique needs; Wawanesa Life, a provider of life insurance products; and Western Financial Group, a leading national distributor of personal and commercial insurance.

Wawanesa is committed to helping communities thrive in a changing world. The company invests more than $4 million annually in charitable initiatives, including $2.5 million each year to support people and communities on the front lines of climate change. Learn more at wawanesa.com.

We are currently seeking dedicated, driven, and enthusiastic individuals who thrive in a dynamic environment, embrace change, and are eager to gain diverse experience while advancing their careers as part of a growing team.

Job Overview

The Director, Personal Lines, Business Planning & Performance is responsible for coordinating business strategy and planning development, providing trusted advice, insights and performance management across the Personal lines of business and key business partners.

This role provides critical support to the SVP & Chief Personal Lines Officer by monitoring market developments and gathering internal and external performance metrics and business insights to enable informed decision-making, identifying opportunities for improvement, and ensuring enterprise-level alignment in planning, reporting, and execution. This role also brings together pertinent information (performance metrics, business insights and market data) into a cohesive view and narrative for the Line of Business for Executive and Board reporting. With direct leadership of cross functional business planning and market monitoring, this role is instrumental in building a performance-focused and member-centric culture. This role requires balancing high-level strategic work with tactical execution, ensuring focus on achieving Wawanesa’s critical goals in the coming years.

Job Responsibilities

Serve as an advisor to the Chief Personal Lines Officer, delivering confidential counsel and perspective on matters of priority to Personal Lines planning and performance across the line of business.
Coordinate the Personal Lines strategic and tactical business planning process, gathering the relevant operational reporting/performance monitoring inputs, ensuring alignment with enterprise planning processes and priorities.
Collaborate closely with executive leadership to translate strategic objectives into measurable initiatives and performance indicators. Oversee the design and execution of executive reporting dashboards, business reviews, and decision-support analytics for the SVP and senior leadership.
Monitor and analyze external competitor and market developments, industry benchmarks, and risk, to present actionable information to support decision-making and prepare the organization to adapt effectively and proactively to changes.
Foster a collaborative environment that brings together sales, operations, finance, compliance, legal, and strategy to address performance and planning needs holistically.
Drive cross-functional initiatives and deliver results by executing through influence, effectively navigating a matrixed structure without direct authority.
Create and manage agendas and execute logistics for Personal Lines Senior Leadership meetings (including strategy and offsite sessions), Personal Lines communication forums (e.g., Townhalls, Ask Anything sessions, etc.) and track follow-ups.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, insurance, actuarial science, analytics, or a related field; MBA or equivalent advanced education is an asset.
Minimum 8–10 years of experience in strategic or business planning, performance reporting, operational leadership or regulatory compliance in the P&C insurance industry.
Proven leadership experience managing cross-functional teams and delivering results in a matrixed environment.
Strong understanding of insurance operations, risk management and industry financial and non-financial performance drivers.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into action, drive execution, and measure impact through well-structured performance frameworks, including analyzing complex issues from multiple angles and provide sound counsel among competing priorities.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with a high degree of comfort working with data, financials, and reporting tools.
Exceptional versatility, agility, situational awareness, and composure. Proven ability to navigate multiple issues concurrently and prioritize critical work.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues from multiple angles and provide sound counsel among competing priorities, including experience in financial literacy and quantitative analysis, with the ability to distill actionable insights.
Effective communicator and collaborator, with strong storytelling and presentation skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
Deep alignment with Wawanesa’s values and purpose, with a passion for supporting people, protecting members, and improving the way we work.
Flexibility to travel within Canada and work variable hours, including overtime, as required.
Agile business mindset with a focus on innovative problem-solving and interdepartmental collaboration.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level correspondence.

Diversity Equity, Inclusion & Belonging

At Wawanesa, we are committed to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) and believe that our strength lies in the diversity of our people – this is supported by having a representative workforce.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including racialized persons, women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender-diverse and neurodiverse individuals, and anyone who can contribute to the further diversification of thought and ideas.

We aim to ensure our recruitment process is accessible to all candidates. If you require accommodations during any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out in confidence to jobs@wawanesa.com.

All Wawanesa job applicants are subject to Wawanesa's Privacy Policy.

Please note that the recruitment process for this position may involve the use of AI tools to screen, assess, or select applicants. All final decisions are taken or reviewed by human recruiters and human hiring leaders in compliance with all applicable legislation.

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
Company Description
Refine Finance provides AI-powered fractional CFO and outsourced accounting services that deliver expert financial guidance at a fraction of the cost of a full-time in-house team. The company helps small and mid-sized businesses automate routine financial tasks, access real-time strategic insights, and make data-driven decisions to support efficient growth. With advanced AI-driven analytics, clients can optimize cash flow, forecast trends, manage risk, and maintain compliance and financial accuracy. Refine Finance serves entrepreneurs and business owners across North America, taking leadership of their finances, operations, and strategy so they can focus on scaling their businesses and ensuring long-term financial health.
Role Description
The Director of Finance and Accounting is a full-time, hybrid role based in the Greater Toronto Area, Canada, with flexibility for some work from home. This role oversees financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and the preparation and review of financial statements and reports. The Director will manage accounting operations, ensure accuracy and compliance with relevant standards and regulations, and optimize internal controls and financial processes. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading and mentoring a finance and accounting team, providing strategic financial insights to support decision-making, partnering with leadership on growth initiatives, and leveraging data and technology to improve efficiency and financial visibility. The Director will also communicate financial performance and risks to stakeholders and contribute to long-term financial strategy and governance.
Qualifications

Strong expertise in Finance and Financial Planning, with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and strategic analysis.
Proficiency in preparing and reviewing Financial Statements and Financial Reporting, including compliance with accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated Analytical Skills and the ability to interpret complex financial data to provide clear, actionable insights.
Proven leadership experience managing finance and accounting teams, including coaching, performance management, and team development.
Advanced skills with financial systems, spreadsheets, and data analysis tools; experience with AI-driven or automated finance platforms is an asset.
Solid understanding of internal controls, audit processes, risk management, and best practices in corporate governance.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present financial information to non-financial stakeholders and build strong cross-functional relationships.
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field; CPA, CFA, or equivalent professional designation strongly preferred.
QBO experience is a must
Project based accounting is a plus

jobs.description:
Our client is a well-established and growing organization in the CPG manufacturing and distribution sector. While they continue to expand their operations, strengthen market presence, and drive long-term growth, they are seeking an accomplished Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join their executive leadership team.
Reporting directly to the President, the CFO will serve as a key strategic partner, providing financial leadership, business insight, and operational support across the organization. This executive will play a critical role in driving profitability, optimizing financial performance, supporting growth initiatives, and ensuring strong financial governance within a fast-paced CPG manufacturing and distribution environment.

Immediate Vacancy
On-site work space

What Our Client Offers
Competitive base salary of $210,000 to $240,000, with flexibility to consider a higher compensation package for an exceptional candidate.
Annual performance-based bonus opportunity of 20% to 25%.
Three weeks of vacation, with the potential for four weeks based on experience and qualifications.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Retirement savings program.

Your Impact in the Company

Lead the organization's overall financial strategy, planning, and performance.
● Provide financial insight and recommendations to the CEO and executive leadership team.
● Oversee budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and cash flow management.
● Drive profitability through margin analysis, cost optimization, and operational efficiencies.

Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, and Distribution teams to support business objectives.

Manage banking relationships, financing activities, and capital planning.

Ensure strong internal controls, risk management, and regulatory compliance.

Lead and develop the Finance and Accounting teams.

Support strategic initiatives, acquisitions, and business growth opportunities.

Qualifications for this position

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; MBA considered an asset.
CPA designation is a strong asset.
10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including experience as a CFO, VP Finance, or equivalent executive-level role.
Experience within the consumer products industry
Strong understanding of cost accounting, inventory management, production costing, and supply chain finance.
Proven success leading financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and business performance management.
Experience managing lender relationships, capital planning, and cash flow optimization.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, corporate governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Strong leadership capabilities with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organization.

About the role

The Director will support the Vice President Sales as a trusted advisor. As a strategic thinker this individual brings operational experience executing on key sales focus areas. The Director is a strategic and critical role responsible for working closely with business development and account expansion leaders to drive key strategic initiatives and delivering profitable solution design. The director leads the analysis and architecture of client solutions by assessing the client’s requirements, developing and validating solution design.

What you’ll be doing

Oversees solution design and provides support for business development and account expansion opportunities.
Assesses client business needs, goals and overall strategic direction.
Leads the analysis and architecture of client solutions.
Develops and validates solution design/blueprint.
Collaborates with internal business partners to develop profitable account design recommendations.
Stays abreast of industry/market knowledge and trends.
Improves the probability of RFP wins for strategic deals by incorporating solution design to create opportunity tailored value propositions for every bid.
Collaborate with Vice President, Sales to ensure execution of agreed goals and initiatives.
Ensure proactive management of key relationships both internally and externally (employees, executives, clients, industry organizations, etc).
Identify pain points throughout the sales organization and optimize processes and procedures to improve efficiencies across teams.
Represent company as required, including at industry events and conferences.
Support the Vice President, Sales in preparation for corporate meetings, and meetings with key external stakeholders, including customers, and strategic partners
Partner with the Vice President, Sales to develop and drive key strategic initiatives that support the long-term growth and success of the business.

About you

Demonstrated ability to work across all levels of the organization to obtain resources and provide support and expertise.
Strong planning, research, and project management skills. Proactive and able to solve problems effectively and rapidly using excellent analytical skills.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

________________________________________

Stakeholder Management

The CFO Will Maintain Productive Relationships With

Internal Stakeholders

Board of Directors
Executive Leadership Team
Department Leaders
Team Members

External Stakeholders

Tsuut'ina Nation Leadership
Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)
Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC)
Auditors
Financial Institutions
Legal Counsel
Development Partners
Government Agencies
Industry Associations
Consultants and Contractors

________________________________________

Risk Management & Governance

Lead enterprise risk management activities.
Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

________________________________________

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

The CFO serves as management's primary liaison to the Finance and Audit Committee and is responsible for:

Preparing committee materials and recommendations.
Presenting financial results and forecasts.
Supporting audit processes.
Monitoring risk management activities.
Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

________________________________________

We thank all applicants, however, only those considered for an interview will be contacted.No phone calls please.

Priority will be given to Tsuut'ina Nation members.

jobs.title: Vice President, Strategy & Innovation
jobs.description:
HSB Canada, part of Munich Re, is Canada's premier engineering-driven specialty insurer and provider of inspection, engineering and technology services that set the standard for excellence in the market. Our constantly evolving offerings lead the market in cyber, equipment breakdown, renewable energy, technology services, engineering based risk management and inspection services. We bring technical expertise to help our clients stay ahead of complex, emerging, and technology-based risks. We dare to think big, and we are continuously innovating on behalf of our clients. We recognize Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging as key priorities and a culture that welcomes different thoughts and opinions.

HSB is much more! It’s insurance. Engineering. Technology. To learn more about us, please visit www.hsb.ca (opens in new window)

Primary Objectives

HSB Canada is seeking a Vice President, Strategy & Innovation to help shape the company's long-term direction and turn strategic ambition into measurable business results. Reporting directly to the President & CEO and serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, this leader will bring quantitative rigor to enterprise strategy, strengthen execution discipline, and build a focused portfolio of innovation opportunities that create customer and business value.

Operating as an internal strategy and innovation consultant, the Vice President will work across business units and functions to frame complex issues, synthesize data and market insight, challenge assumptions, align senior stakeholders, and mobilize cross-functional teams. The role will also refresh HSB Canada's Internet of Things (IoT) strategy and go-to-market approach, strengthening the connection between technology-enabled services, insurance solutions, distribution opportunities, and customer needs.

The successful candidate will build strong cross-functional partnerships with HSB and Munich Re Group business leaders and enterprise partners to align priorities, remove barriers, and accelerate priorities ensuring understanding of relevant strategy, standards and philosophy.

Internal Applicants please apply online and submit your candidacy by October 14, 2026.

External Applicants please apply online and submit your candidacy by October 31,2026.

Job Responsibilities

Enterprise Strategy and Strategic Planning
Lead enterprise strategic planning with the President & CEO and Executive Leadership Team, including strategy refreshes, scenarios, priorities, and roadmaps.
Shape evidence-based choices on growth, portfolio priorities, partnerships, investments, and emerging risks.
Translate strategy into measurable objectives, initiatives, milestones, accountabilities, and resource priorities.
Advise and challenge senior leaders, and develop clear Board materials on choices, trade-offs, progress, and decisions.
Business Performance and Execution Discipline
Co-lead quarterly business reviews with FP&A, linking strategic priorities to financial and operating performance.
Hold business leaders accountable for commitments, indicators, dependencies, corrective actions, and outcomes.
Establish practical execution disciplines, including scorecards, governance, benefits tracking, and escalation.
Use quantitative analysis to identify gaps, size opportunities, evaluate trade-offs, and recommend action, while respecting FP&A ownership of core financial processes.
Innovation Portfolio and Commercialization
Build and manage an innovation portfolio aligned with strategy, customer needs, financial goals, risk appetite, and capacity.
Identify and incubate new products, services, digital and data solutions, partnerships, and business models.
Govern opportunities from validation and business case through pilot, commercialization, and value realization.
Equip business leaders with disciplined innovation practices and recommend when to advance, pivot, pause, or stop initiatives.
IoT Strategy and Go-to-Market Leadership
Refresh HSB Canada’s IoT strategy, positioning, target segments, value propositions, ecosystem, and investment priorities.
Develop a go-to-market roadmap linking IoT-enabled risk solutions to underwriting, distribution, client needs, service delivery, and value creation.
Mobilize business, functional, and Group partners to move priority IoT opportunities from strategy to market.
Define measures for adoption, customer value, risk improvement, revenue, and profitability.
Market Insight, Executive Advisory and Group Integration
Turn customer, broker, competitor, technology, regulatory, and economic insights into actionable recommendations.
Align HSB Canada, HSB, and Munich Re Group stakeholders around shared outcomes, decisions, and timelines.
Lead high-priority cross-enterprise projects requiring structured problem solving, executive sponsorship, and coordinated execution.
Deliver Board-ready communications, represent HSB Canada in Group forums, and translate Group capabilities into Canadian opportunities.
People Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop up to five professionals across strategy, innovation, market insight, and portfolio management.
Set clear priorities, delegate ownership, provide timely feedback, and hold the team accountable for results.
Build diverse talent and foster curiosity, constructive challenge, experimentation, and learning.
Influence and mobilize matrixed teams beyond direct reporting lines.

Qualifications

Experience and Education

Approximately 12 or more years of progressive experience in enterprise strategy, corporate strategy, management consulting, innovation, business transformation, corporate development, or a related field, including significant leadership experience.
A record of advising CEOs and senior executives, leading enterprise planning, solving ambiguous business problems, and converting strategy into execution.
Experience building and governing innovation portfolios and bringing products, services, or new ventures from insight through commercialization.
Demonstrated people leadership, including coaching strong talent, setting priorities, and driving accountability across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Prior experience with a leading management consulting firm is a strong asset.
Experience in property and casualty insurance, reinsurance, or broader financial services is an asset; experience in another regulated, data-intensive sector may also be relevant.
A bachelor’s degree in business, economics, finance, engineering, mathematics, or a related discipline is required. An MBA or other relevant graduate degree is an asset.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic agility: Quickly grasps complex concepts, identifies the critical question, connects disparate information, and develops clear strategic choices.
Quantitative and commercial acumen: Extrapolates insight from financial, operating, customer, and market data; builds robust business cases; and understands value drivers and trade-offs.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
new_jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

Supporting governance best practices.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Strategy & Innovation
new_jobs.description:
HSB Canada, part of Munich Re, is Canada's premier engineering-driven specialty insurer and provider of inspection, engineering and technology services that set the standard for excellence in the market. Our constantly evolving offerings lead the market in cyber, equipment breakdown, renewable energy, technology services, engineering based risk management and inspection services. We bring technical expertise to help our clients stay ahead of complex, emerging, and technology-based risks. We dare to think big, and we are continuously innovating on behalf of our clients. We recognize Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging as key priorities and a culture that welcomes different thoughts and opinions.

HSB is much more! It’s insurance. Engineering. Technology. To learn more about us, please visit www.hsb.ca (opens in new window)

Primary Objectives

HSB Canada is seeking a Vice President, Strategy & Innovation to help shape the company's long-term direction and turn strategic ambition into measurable business results. Reporting directly to the President & CEO and serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, this leader will bring quantitative rigor to enterprise strategy, strengthen execution discipline, and build a focused portfolio of innovation opportunities that create customer and business value.

Operating as an internal strategy and innovation consultant, the Vice President will work across business units and functions to frame complex issues, synthesize data and market insight, challenge assumptions, align senior stakeholders, and mobilize cross-functional teams. The role will also refresh HSB Canada's Internet of Things (IoT) strategy and go-to-market approach, strengthening the connection between technology-enabled services, insurance solutions, distribution opportunities, and customer needs.

The successful candidate will build strong cross-functional partnerships with HSB and Munich Re Group business leaders and enterprise partners to align priorities, remove barriers, and accelerate priorities ensuring understanding of relevant strategy, standards and philosophy.

Internal Applicants please apply online and submit your candidacy by October 14, 2026.

External Applicants please apply online and submit your candidacy by October 31,2026.

Job Responsibilities

Enterprise Strategy and Strategic Planning
Lead enterprise strategic planning with the President & CEO and Executive Leadership Team, including strategy refreshes, scenarios, priorities, and roadmaps.
Shape evidence-based choices on growth, portfolio priorities, partnerships, investments, and emerging risks.
Translate strategy into measurable objectives, initiatives, milestones, accountabilities, and resource priorities.
Advise and challenge senior leaders, and develop clear Board materials on choices, trade-offs, progress, and decisions.
Business Performance and Execution Discipline
Co-lead quarterly business reviews with FP&A, linking strategic priorities to financial and operating performance.
Hold business leaders accountable for commitments, indicators, dependencies, corrective actions, and outcomes.
Establish practical execution disciplines, including scorecards, governance, benefits tracking, and escalation.
Use quantitative analysis to identify gaps, size opportunities, evaluate trade-offs, and recommend action, while respecting FP&A ownership of core financial processes.
Innovation Portfolio and Commercialization
Build and manage an innovation portfolio aligned with strategy, customer needs, financial goals, risk appetite, and capacity.
Identify and incubate new products, services, digital and data solutions, partnerships, and business models.
Govern opportunities from validation and business case through pilot, commercialization, and value realization.
Equip business leaders with disciplined innovation practices and recommend when to advance, pivot, pause, or stop initiatives.
IoT Strategy and Go-to-Market Leadership
Refresh HSB Canada’s IoT strategy, positioning, target segments, value propositions, ecosystem, and investment priorities.
Develop a go-to-market roadmap linking IoT-enabled risk solutions to underwriting, distribution, client needs, service delivery, and value creation.
Mobilize business, functional, and Group partners to move priority IoT opportunities from strategy to market.
Define measures for adoption, customer value, risk improvement, revenue, and profitability.
Market Insight, Executive Advisory and Group Integration
Turn customer, broker, competitor, technology, regulatory, and economic insights into actionable recommendations.
Align HSB Canada, HSB, and Munich Re Group stakeholders around shared outcomes, decisions, and timelines.
Lead high-priority cross-enterprise projects requiring structured problem solving, executive sponsorship, and coordinated execution.
Deliver Board-ready communications, represent HSB Canada in Group forums, and translate Group capabilities into Canadian opportunities.
People Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop up to five professionals across strategy, innovation, market insight, and portfolio management.
Set clear priorities, delegate ownership, provide timely feedback, and hold the team accountable for results.
Build diverse talent and foster curiosity, constructive challenge, experimentation, and learning.
Influence and mobilize matrixed teams beyond direct reporting lines.

Qualifications

Experience and Education

Approximately 12 or more years of progressive experience in enterprise strategy, corporate strategy, management consulting, innovation, business transformation, corporate development, or a related field, including significant leadership experience.
A record of advising CEOs and senior executives, leading enterprise planning, solving ambiguous business problems, and converting strategy into execution.
Experience building and governing innovation portfolios and bringing products, services, or new ventures from insight through commercialization.
Demonstrated people leadership, including coaching strong talent, setting priorities, and driving accountability across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Prior experience with a leading management consulting firm is a strong asset.
Experience in property and casualty insurance, reinsurance, or broader financial services is an asset; experience in another regulated, data-intensive sector may also be relevant.
A bachelor’s degree in business, economics, finance, engineering, mathematics, or a related discipline is required. An MBA or other relevant graduate degree is an asset.

Strategic agility: Quickly grasps complex concepts, identifies the critical question, connects disparate information, and develops clear strategic choices.
Quantitative and commercial acumen: Extrapolates insight from financial, operating, customer, and market data; builds robust business cases; and understands value drivers and trade-offs.
